payload.reason: The evidence provides specific methods and techniques used to identify non-standard pronunciation in speech recognition systems.

claims.text: Non-standard pronunciation is identified through annotations for mispronunciations, poor intelligibility, and other disfluencies in transcriptions.
The use of phonetic lexicons and character-to-phoneme approximations helps in identifying pronunciation errors, as evidenced by varying error rates in speech recognition tasks.
Standardized procedures for aligning text to audio help identify segments with misalignments, which may indicate non-standard pronunciations.
